newsitem.title: UK: EU demands few concessions for BT/MCI merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: EU demands few concessions for BT/MCI merger - paper.

text.p: The European Commission is demanding only two substantial concessions from British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp of the U.S. in return for approval of their $20 billion merger, a British newspaper reported on Friday.

BT will be required to modify its dominant position in the British audio and video conferencing market, and will have to guarantee access for competitors to its transatlantic submarine cable, the Financial Times said.

BT on Thursday expressed confidence that the merger would be cleared, while a Commission source said the European Union executive would probably be able to rule on the deal ahead of its June 11 deadline.
The Commission began a full probe into the merger in January, saying it was concerned that it might harm fair competition on the route between the U.S. and Britain, as well as the U.S.-Europe route.
EU Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert said last month that the link-up would be cleared if the firms proposed "remedies to competition problems".
